reviewer.method: Sole reader-4 successor personally read all six original publisher PDF pages, complete two-panel pedigree, entire Table 1 with all columns/footnotes, and all nine references; all six page renders inspected. audit.exposure_note: Conservative per_case declaration: mandatory HANDOFF and inherited project/report context exposed historical public control and per-case narratives before this succession. No inference-output file, target-case ranking, or per-case outcome was opened or consulted for this seven-paper audit. This review is post-inference and not blinded.

identity.title: Phenotypic variability in RERE-related disorders and the first report of an inherited variant
identity.note: Original DOI10.1002/ajmg.a.62952 and title/authors match exact-PMID identity. Six original pages confirmed by PDF metadata and full reading.

evidence.locator: Entire six-page original: Figure1 on p.3360; Table1 on p.3362; final declarations/reference list p.3363

component_inventory.note: One two-panel main pedigree figure and one main table. Full paper contains no supplemental file citation or supplemental section. Author-held data are explicitly restricted/request-only and are not silently counted as an available supplement; no request made.

coverage.locator: Abstract through conclusion, all declarations and nine complete reference entries; layout extraction checked against original page renders

components.note: All text and all six page images actually inspected. Reference-list reading does not imply separate reading of the cited articles.

components.note: Figure1b maps case2 to III-2 and case3 to II-2. Maternal uncle is II-3 in the actual figure; prose refers to III-3, which labels an unaffected sister in the figure. No variant carriage inferred from unshaded symbols.

patient_identity.statement: Case2 is the four-year-old male III-2, matching packet sex/age/identity.

genotype.statement: Source reports heterozygous NM_012102.3:c.1512dup, p.Tyr505Valfs*37. Packet uses NM_001042681.2 and NP_001036146.1 with the same c./protein change, plus genomic/VCF coordinates not printed in the source.
limitations: Transcript accession substitution and NC_000001.11:g.8364777dup versus chr1:8364773 A>AC normalization were not independently verified; do not claim exact reference-coordinate equivalence.

segregation.statement: Clinical trio exome sequencing identifies the variant in the child and mother; maternal inheritance is explicitly reported.

phase.statement: Single heterozygous allele is reported. Maternal transmission is documented for the child; no cis/trans two-allele question is present.
limitations: No independent read-level phasing performed; origin of the allele in case3 remains unknown.

causal_confidence.statement: The packet labels the familial variant PATHOGENIC; the source explicitly classifies it as likely pathogenic. The paper predicts nonsense-mediated decay and states it has no direct functional evidence for the proposed mechanism.

evidence.locator: End of §3.2/start p.3361; §3.3 p.3361; Table1 header p.3362; Discussion p.3361

limitations: Formal source-label mismatch, not an independent reclassification or a claim that the variant is benign. Mild phenotype and family/environmental alternatives limit causal certainty.

phenotype_completeness.statement: Case2 packet excludes epicanthus despite explicit bilateral epicanthal folds. It also upgrades mild sinus dilation to aortic root aneurysm and encodes many unassessed features as exclusions.
limitations: Detailed negative terms are individually unresolved unless supported by an actual assessment. Empty Table1 cells are not negative results.

assessment.statement: RERE symbol, heterozygosity, c.1512dup and predicted p.Tyr505Valfs*37 correspond; the packet changes transcript accession and adds unreported genomic/VCF coordinates.
limitations: Source NM_012102.3; packet NM_001042681.2/NP_001036146.1. No independent transcript/genomic normalization.

limitations: Conservative per_case declaration: mandatory HANDOFF and inherited project/report context exposed historical public control and per-case narratives before this succession. No inference-output file, target-case ranking, or per-case outcome was opened or consulted for this seven-paper audit. This review is post-inference and not blinded.
